findings.statement: Bitquery counts 7,821,066 account-to-account RLUSD payments from 19 September to 18 October; 7,789,341 (99.6%) went from a 110-wallet cluster to three collectors and carried only 7,722 RLUSD in total. The cluster is inferred from shared funding and receivers, not identified beneficial owners.
findings.disconfirming_evidence: The remaining 14,600 payments of at least 1 RLUSD moved $7.33B gross; the high-value flow is materially different from the dust cluster.

findings.statement: The exact address rDAE53VfMvftPB4ogpWGWvzkQxfht6JPxr is identified by Bitquery as the RLUSD cluster's Binance-labelled funding wallet and by Bithomp as the source of 185,017,485.5 XRP sent to the incident receiver at 20:05 UTC on 29 October. This is an address match, not a common-actor finding.
findings.disconfirming_evidence: Bitquery says the bot pattern fits one Binance customer rather than Binance itself; an exchange omnibus wallet can serve unrelated customers. The bot cluster shut down 13–15 days before the incident.

findings.statement: After the 185M XRP transfer, rDAE53 sent 11,141,435.843 XRP to Bithomp-labelled Binance account rs8Z at 23:12:20 UTC on 29 October, then 51,172,508 RLUSD to the same destination at 01:27:10 UTC on 30 October. These are confirmed successful payments between explorer-labelled accounts; they do not establish replenishment or recovery.
findings.disconfirming_evidence: No official Binance statement or raw PoR export identifies the destination as a reserve-replenishment account; account labels do not prove beneficial ownership.

findings.statement: At retrieval, Bithomp page bodies displayed 11.59 XRP for rDAE53 and 8.60 XRP for each of the four other incident source accounts, a body-derived aggregate of 45.99 XRP. The page title summaries display 12.99 and 10.00 XRP respectively, a 7 XRP aggregate discrepancy. Raw account_info is still required.
findings.disconfirming_evidence: Bithomp title/body values conflict; no second explorer or raw validated account_info result was obtained.

findings.statement: The $7.33B of RLUSD payments of at least 1 RLUSD includes $728M issuer-to-mint-wallet and $744M redemption-to-issuer flows, plus a separate $424M each-way wallet roundtrip. Those $2.32B gross components are approximately 31.65% of reported gross volume and are not net new external capital.
findings.disconfirming_evidence: Other large transfers may represent genuine settlement or rebalancing; beneficial owners and economic purpose of most addresses remain unknown.

findings.statement: After dust removal, Bitquery reports 14,600 payments, 1,826 senders and 1,536 receivers, $7.33B gross value and a 150 RLUSD median. Ten senders moved $6.05B (about 82.5%); 828 payments of at least $1M moved $6.98B (about 95.2%).
findings.disconfirming_evidence: Public transfers do not reveal beneficial ownership, net external capital or final economic settlement; exchange/custody omnibus behavior and issuer plumbing are included.

findings.statement: The bot cluster began shutting down at 17:00 UTC on 14 October; the first collector's last payment was 03:44 UTC on 15 October and the second collector dropped sharply at 03:00 UTC on 16 October. Cross River announced its RLUSD integration on 15 October. Bitquery found no ledger event explaining the shutdown.
findings.disconfirming_evidence: No transaction fee spike or ledger amendment explains the timing; coincidence or an off-chain decision remain plausible.

findings.statement: Bitquery estimates 495 XRP in fees for 8,602,917 transactions, about $648 at its 19 October valuation price of $1.31. This is a network-usage cost, not evidence of material XRP acquisition or price demand.
findings.disconfirming_evidence: Fees are a real XRP-denominated network cost, but the amount is tiny relative to market turnover and the 233.46M XRP incident transfer.

competing_hypotheses.claim: The headline RLUSD payment count materially overstates organic XRPL adoption during 19 September–18 October because 99.6% of the counted payments were attributed to a 110-wallet dust cluster.
supporting_evidence: 7,789,341 of 7,821,066 payments went to three collectors and carried only 7,722 RLUSD.
The cluster was funded from Binance-labelled wallets and paid 495 XRP in fees for 8.6M transactions.
disconfirming_evidence: 14,600 payments of at least 1 RLUSD moved $7.33B gross.
1,826 senders and 1,536 receivers appear in the high-value sample.
unknowns: Beneficial owners of high-value senders and receivers.
Economic purpose and net external settlement of the $7.33B gross flows.

competing_hypotheses.claim: Gross RLUSD transfer value overstates net new capital because issuer mint/redemption plumbing and a matched two-wallet roundtrip contribute approximately $2.32B (31.65%) of the $7.33B gross total.
supporting_evidence: Issuer mint/redemption flows total approximately $1.472B gross.
A wallet pair passed $424M each way, adding $848M gross without an external payee.
disconfirming_evidence: The remaining transfers may represent real settlement, exchange/custody movements or rebalancing; beneficial owners are unknown.
unknowns: Net flows among independent beneficial owners.
How much of the remaining $5.01B represents economic settlement versus omnibus/custody movement.

competing_hypotheses.claim: The shared rDAE53 address connects the RLUSD bot-funding analysis to one of the five XRP incident source wallets, but does not connect the bot operator to the theft actor.
supporting_evidence: Bitquery identifies rDAE53 as the RLUSD funding source for 109 bot wallets.
Bithomp records 185,017,485.5 XRP from the same address to the incident receiver at 20:05 UTC on 29 October.
disconfirming_evidence: Bitquery says the pattern fits one Binance customer rather than Binance itself.
The cluster shutdown was 13–15 days before the XRP incident.
An exchange omnibus wallet can serve unrelated customers.
unknowns: Beneficial owner of the bot cluster.
Whether any operational account or customer links the cluster to the incident actor.

competing_hypotheses.claim: Post-incident XRP and RLUSD transfers from rDAE53 to another Binance-labelled account indicate that the source account continued to make successful payments after the 185M XRP transfer.
supporting_evidence: 11,141,435.843 XRP moved to rs8Z at 23:12:20 UTC on 29 October.
51,172,508 RLUSD moved to rs8Z at 01:27:10 UTC on 30 October.
disconfirming_evidence: These could be routine sweeps or rebalancing; labels do not prove ownership or who controlled signing at each moment.
unknowns: Whether access was continuously retained or recovered.
Whether any post-incident movement represented reserve replenishment.

competing_hypotheses.claim: The Cross River RLUSD integration announcement caused the 110-wallet bot cluster to shut down.
supporting_evidence: The first collector's inflow fell on 14 October and its last payment was early 15 October; Cross River announced on 15 October; the second collector fell sharply on 16 October.
disconfirming_evidence: Bitquery found no fee spike, ledger amendment or other ledger event explaining the shutdown and explicitly says timing alone cannot identify a cause.
unknowns: Off-chain decision, operator intent, or unrelated operational cause.

competing_hypotheses.claim: Binance itself operated the 110-wallet RLUSD bot cluster.
supporting_evidence: The wallets were funded through Binance-labelled exchange wallets.
disconfirming_evidence: Bitquery explicitly states the flow pattern fits one Binance customer rather than Binance itself.
No direct Binance operation, instruction or beneficial-owner evidence is presented.
unknowns: Identity of the customer or operator.

next_actions: Obtain raw validated XRPL account_info for all five Binance-labelled source accounts and reconcile the Bithomp title/body discrepancy.
Refresh the attacker receiver and its complete post-06:43 UTC transaction history; preserve exact ledger indexes and timestamps.
Crosswalk rDAE53, the other four source accounts and rs8Z against the official Binance October 1 PoR address export; do not substitute explorer labels.
Trace the RLUSD collector-to-deposit-account loop and separate gross transfer value, issuer mint/redemption, matched roundtrips, exchange/custody omnibus flows and net external settlement.
Keep the bot cluster as an anomaly label; do not use raw RLUSD payment count as organic adoption or XRP demand.
Continue fixed-horizon XRP feature-store work only after synchronized venue, ETF, funding, OI, liquidity and event data pass quality checks.
